trends: The current technology landscape is characterized by a significant push towards highly efficient and accessible AI, particularly in the realm of Large Language Models (LLMs) that can run on resource-constrained devices (e.g., single CPUs, minimal RAM) and are often reimplemented in performance-focused languages like C or Rust. This efficiency is a cornerstone for the emergence of sophisticated, agentic automation systems capable of understanding intent, recording user actions, and executing multi-step tasks across diverse platforms. These agents are being applied to complex real-world problems, from legal compliance to enterprise document extraction. Concurrently, there's a strong emphasis on developer productivity, with a shift in focus from low-level coding to higher-level orchestration, leveraging AI tools, and embracing emergent design principles where problems are designed to dissolve rather than explicitly solved, enabling developers to build more by writing less code.

ideas.title: Local AI Workflow Automation & Skill Generator
ideas.description: Develop a desktop application that acts as an AI-powered 'skill recorder' for local workflows. The application will observe user interactions (mouse clicks, keyboard inputs, application usage) for a specific task. Using a locally running LLM (e.g., via Ollama, Llama.cpp), it will analyze the recorded session to infer the user's intent and break down the task into an ordered sequence of reusable steps. The system will then generate a runnable automation script (e.g., Python or shell script) or a 'skill' definition that can be executed to repeat the task. This project enhances developer productivity by transforming repetitive actions into automated processes, without relying on cloud-based AI services, ensuring privacy and cost-effectiveness.
tech_stack: Python (for backend logic, desktop interaction capture via pyautogui/pynput)
A scripting language for generated automations (e.g., Python, PowerShell, Bash)
ideas.source_inspiration: microsoft/skill-recorder, Yerensoncasares/termux-dev-station, TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving, I Built a Chat App That Rewrites Its Own UI in Real Time
steps: Design and implement a desktop application UI for recording, managing, and executing skills.
Integrate desktop event capturing (mouse, keyboard, active window) into the application.
Set up local LLM inference using Ollama or Llama.cpp to process recorded events.
Develop logic for the LLM to analyze recorded sequences, infer intent, and generate step-by-step descriptions.
Implement a code generation module that translates LLM-generated steps into executable automation scripts.
Add a 'playback' feature to execute the generated scripts and a user feedback loop for refinement.

ideas.title: Domain-Specific, Ultra-Efficient Micro-LLM
ideas.description: Create an extremely parameter-efficient (e.g., < 50M parameters) language model fine-tuned for a highly specific domain, such as IoT device command interpretation, short-form code snippet generation, or medical symptom classification. The core focus is on achieving competitive accuracy for the narrow domain while ensuring minimal resource footprint (RAM, CPU cycles) for local or edge deployment. This involves exploring model architectures like Kimi K3 or BarunLM-35M, and potentially reimplementing or optimizing inference in C/Rust for maximum performance. This project addresses the trend of making powerful AI accessible on resource-constrained hardware, enabling offline and private AI applications.
tech_stack: C/C++/Rust (for highly optimized inference engine, potentially from scratch)
Knowledge of efficient model architectures (e.g., Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
ideas.source_inspiration: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c, harrrshall/barunlm-35m, melonmath/microkimi, TimRots/kimi3, Autoregressive Language Model on the 6502 Processor
steps: Select a niche domain with available datasets for training a small language model.
Research and choose an efficient base model architecture (or design a new one) that fits parameter constraints.
Curate and preprocess a high-quality, domain-specific dataset for fine-tuning.
Train or fine-tune the micro-LLM on the selected dataset, focusing on minimizing parameters and maximizing performance.
Implement or adapt a highly optimized inference engine in C or Rust for the trained model.
Develop a lightweight API or CLI for testing and demonstrating the model's capabilities on target hardware.

ideas.title: Schema-Guided Intelligent Document Processor
ideas.description: Build an intelligent agent that can extract structured information from various document types (PDFs, scanned images, text files) based on a user-defined schema (e.g., JSON, YAML). The agent should leverage Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) principles with local or API-based LLMs to accurately populate the schema fields. It should handle complex documents, multi-page contexts, and provide a user interface for schema definition, document upload, and extracted data review/correction. This project directly aligns with the need for robust enterprise automation and intelligent data extraction, reducing manual effort and improving data quality in complex workflows.
tech_stack: LangChain/LlamaIndex (for agentic workflow and RAG implementation)
OCR libraries (e.g., Tesseract, PaddleOCR) or commercial APIs (e.g., Google Cloud Vision, Azure AI Vision) for text extraction from images/PDFs.
Local LLM (e.g., via Ollama) or API-based LLM (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) for extraction and reasoning.
Web framework (Flask/FastAPI) for API, and a frontend framework (e.g., React, Vue) for the UI.
ideas.source_inspiration: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction, Labour-Law-Violation-System, TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
steps: Design the user interface for schema definition (JSON/YAML input) and document upload.
Implement document parsing capabilities (PDF, image, text) using OCR and text extraction libraries.
Integrate a RAG pipeline: chunk documents, create vector embeddings, and store them.
Develop an agentic LLM prompt engineering strategy to guide extraction based on the user-defined schema.
Implement a robust extraction and validation mechanism, allowing for human review and correction.
Build an API layer and integrate the UI for seamless document processing and structured data output.

quick_actions: Dedicate 15 minutes today to install and run a small local LLM (e.g., Llama 3 via Ollama) on your machine. Experiment with basic prompts to understand its capabilities and resource usage firsthand.

Identify one recurring, manual task in your daily developer workflow. Spend 30 minutes sketching out a step-by-step automation plan for it, considering how an AI agent could augment or fully handle each step.

Read the Dev.to article 'I Haven't Written Code in 8 Months. I've Never Built More.' and reflect on how you can shift your focus from writing raw code to orchestrating tools and leveraging AI for higher-level problem-solving.

Explore a visual automation builder like n8n or Make (formerly Integromat). Try connecting a simple trigger (e.g., new email) to an AI action (e.g., summarization) and then to another action (e.g., save to a note app) to experience no-code agentic workflows.
